content.comment_body: Hello! I have questions about communication and uploading programs between [product_name] and a PC. I'm currently using [product_name] with article number [article_no], and [product_name] version [version_no]. Which hardware type should I select? Is it the [product_name] version [version_no]? I've attached my software, where I want to display the analog value (Vout) from a simulated sensor (a short circuit oscillating between 0-10V, controlled by potentiometers). I want this value shown on the [product_name]'s display. The problem is that the display only shows 1 or 2, changing randomly regardless of the actual Vout value. I'm using ethernet communication: [product_name] IP: 192.168.1.3, PC IP: 192.168.1.6, Gateway: 192.168.0.1. Vout is connected directly to I1 (AI1).

Yes, for hardware selection you need to choose [product_name] version [version_no]. Which terminal did you connect the 0-10V signal to? Was it I7? I7 serves as AI1 (it's labeled as such on the device). Is the OV of the signal connected to the M of the module's supply voltage?

Have you changed the IP address of the [product_name] on the device itself? By default, the IP address is 192.168.0.3, with a subnet mask of 255.255.255.0. Is there a specific reason you assigned a gateway address?
Thank you for your reply! I connected Vout to I7 now, and that resolved the issue — it was simply a matter of changing the connection.
Glad to hear it's working now.

analysis.insight_summary: The user faced challenges displaying a 0-10V analog signal on the [product_name] screen due to incorrect wiring of the analog input. The confusion involved proper hardware selection in the software and which terminals to use for connecting the analog signal. Community advice led to the user correcting the connection, thereby solving the issue.
analysis.user_expectations: The user expects the [product_name] module to accurately display real-time analog voltage values (Vout) on its screen, and seeks software hardware selection to be straightforward and intuitive.
